rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a CVD Cu coating on W particles followed by SPS consolidation, whereas the paper uses liquid-metal dealloying of a WTaVTi RHEA precursor in molten Cu to create a bicontinuous RHEA–Cu composite. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies SPS under inert atmosphere and fusion-relevant service, while the paper uses vacuum-sealed silica ampoule immersion in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h and measures thermal conductivity up to ~800 °C with He+ irradiation screening. The processing routes and test conditions are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes improved wetting and diffusion bonding via a conformal Cu coating to reduce voids, whereas the paper's mechanism relies on selective Ti dissolution from interdendritic channels, W-rich interlayer passivation, and aligned Cu channels for conductivity. These are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts lower void content, improved bonding, higher thermal conductivity, and better mechanical durability versus conventional W–Cu composites. The paper predicts and measures substantially increased thermal conductivity versus the RHEA precursor, surpassing pure W at high temperature, and reduced He swelling versus pure W. The predicted properties and baselines differ.
